proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Using the stratification U = Z_0 superset Z_1 superset Z_2 superset ... of lemma-finite-stratify, one constructs disjoint unions W = coprod_{r >= 1} W_r and W' = coprod_{r >= 1} W'_r with W'_r a thickening of the R-invariant subscheme W_r, such that the restrictions (W'_r, R'_r, s'_r, t'_r, c'_r) have finite locally free source and target of rank r. The base case sets W_1 = W'_1 = U without Z_1, which is R-invariant open, a thickening with isomorphic hence rank 1 finite locally free restriction, and every point of U without Z_1 lies in t(s^{-1}(W_1 closure)). The inductive step assumes disjoint invariant W_1, ..., W_n with the covering property on U without Z_n, thickening, and rank r finite locally free restrictions; then W_{n+1} is defined set theoretically and W'_{n+1} scheme theoretically as Z_n minus Z_{n+1} and the union of the t(s^{-1}(W_r closures)) for r <= n. Openness of W_{n+1} uses that Z_{n+1} minus the closure of U without Z_{n+1} is open, that this closure lies in the closed subset being removed, and that t is a closed morphism; W'_{n+1} is a closed subscheme of W_{n+1} with the same underlying space by the two ways of taking the difference; properties (1), (2), (3) are immediate and (5) is lemma-finite-stratify. Since the strata have empty intersection, every point of U lies outside some Z_n, whence U = union of the t(s^{-1}(W_r closures)) set theoretically and (2) holds, so W' inside W satisfies (1) through (4). (source lines 2685-2745)

standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the stratification that drives the construction, the rank r finite locally free property (5) on the new stratum, and the empty intersection that yields the covering property (2).

core_obligations: Set up the construction of disjoint unions W = coprod_{r >= 1} W_r and W' = coprod_{r >= 1} W'_r of R-invariant subschemes with W'_r a thickening of W_r and rank r finite locally free restrictions (proof lines 2689-2694). Base case: W_1 = W'_1 = U without Z_1 is R-invariant open, a thickening whose restriction has s', t' isomorphisms, hence finite locally free of rank 1, and every point of U without Z_1 lies in t(s^{-1}(W_1 closure)) (proof lines 2695-2700). Inductive step: assume W_1, ..., W_n disjoint, R-invariant, covering U without Z_n set theoretically by the t(s^{-1}(W_r closures)), each W_r a thickening of W'_r with rank r finite locally free restrictions (proof lines 2703-2713). Define W_{n+1} set theoretically and W'_{n+1} scheme theoretically as Z_n minus Z_{n+1} and the union of the earlier t(s^{-1}(W_r closures)) (proof lines 2714-2727). Openness of W_{n+1} in U follows because Z_{n+1} minus the closure of U without Z_{n+1} is open and that closure is contained in the closed subset being removed, using property (3) of the hypothesis and closedness of t; W'_{n+1} is a closed subscheme of W_{n+1} with the same underlying topological space, properties (1), (2), (3) are clear and (5) is lemma-finite-stratify (proof lines 2728-2736). Conclusion: the strata intersect trivially by lemma-finite-stratify, so every point of U lies in U without Z_n for some n, giving U = union of the t(s^{-1}(W_r closures)) set theoretically and property (2); thus W' inside W satisfies (1), (2), (3) and (4) (proof lines 2738-2744).
proof_roadmap: State the construction target: disjoint unions W and W' of R-invariant pieces with thickenings and rank r finite locally free restrictions (proof lines 2689-2694).
Base case on the first stratum difference W_1 = W'_1 = U without Z_1: invariance, thickening, rank 1 restriction, and the trapping property (proof lines 2695-2700).

Inductive construction of W_{n+1} and W'_{n+1} as set and scheme theoretic differences of Z_n, with openness from closedness of t, the thickening property, and properties (1) through (5) (proof lines 2703-2736).
Conclude with the empty intersection of the strata giving the set theoretic covering U = t(s^{-1}(W closure)) and the four listed properties (proof lines 2738-2744).
